headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces, but dbt-core can egress to a warehouse while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API calls, while python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, screen capture, or MCP surfaces. With no shared channel, the pair cannot pass attacker-controlled instructions by default.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, file bridge, or MCP server is added between the agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF dbt-core begins parsing content from python-cheatsheet as instructions, severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared clipboard and file mounts.
Do not route python-cheatsheet output into dbt-core as executable instructions.
Review any future MCP or message-queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no file, clipboard, or network surfaces. There is no documented shared workspace or direct data path, so leakage is limited unless an operator manually copies sensitive outputs into the docs agent.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs warehouse data into a shared file or clipboard, leakage risk increases.
IF python-cheatsheet is connected to any external API or file reader, reassess as higher severity.
mitigations: Avoid copying warehouse outputs into the documentation agent.
Keep sensitive dbt artifacts in a separate workspace.
Disable any future file-sharing bridge between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are present. dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API calls, while python-cheatsheet has no filesystem write, git modification, or subprocess capability and supports only documentation use. Without shared mutable resources, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess conflict risk.
IF dbt-core gains filesystem write to shared artifacts, severity increases.
mitigations: Do not grant dbt-core shared filesystem write access without locking.
Separate any future mutable resources by agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing outputs, but python-cheatsheet is a reference/documentation agent with no action-taking or execution surfaces. That makes a harmful cascade unlikely unless an operator manually treats dbt output as authoritative instructions for the docs agent or downstream systems.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is used to transform dbt output into operational instructions, reassess as medium or higher.
IF dbt-core output is consumed by an automated executor, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on dbt-generated outputs.
Keep python-cheatsheet in a read-only advisory role.
Document that neither agent should auto-trigger downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, so compliance depends on the warehouse data class and residency controls. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so it is not the compliance driver here. The pair shows no direct residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, but the warehouse path warrants basic review.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data and dbt-core is used outside approved residency boundaries, reassess compliance severity.
IF python-cheatsheet begins handling regulated data, add a separate compliance review.
mitigations: Confirm the warehouse data class before use.
Keep regulated datasets out of any non-approved workflow.
Record the intended residency for dbt runs.
